claim: OpenAI documents the tool-calling interaction as a multi-step flow: provide tools, receive a call, execute application code, return tool output, and receive a final answer or more calls.
notes: Current official API guide checked 2026-11-21; describes the application-side execution boundary.

claim: OpenAI strict function calling requires additionalProperties=false for each object and every property to be required; optional semantics need schema-compatible representation.
notes: Provider-specific schema behavior; do not generalize this exact constraint to every vendor.

claim: Anthropic client tools return tool_use blocks and stop_reason tool_use; the application runs the tool and sends tool_result, while server tools may execute on Anthropic infrastructure.
locator: How tool use works; client and server tools
notes: Current official Anthropic platform documentation checked 2026-11-21.

claim: Toolformer trains a language model to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to incorporate returned results into future token prediction.
notes: Primary paper; historical research result, not a claim about current hosted model behavior.

claim: ToolLLM reports ToolBench with 16,464 real-world RESTful APIs across 49 categories, plus instruction construction, solution-path annotation and ToolEval.
notes: Paper-reported dataset statistics; not a current API catalogue size.

claim: Gorilla combines API-call generation with document retrieval to adapt to changing API documentation and introduces APIBench using Hugging Face, TorchHub and TensorHub APIs.
notes: Primary paper; retrieval is discussed as a way to ground API use in changing documentation.

claim: Anthropic Advanced Tool Use describes on-demand tool discovery, programmatic tool calling and tool-use examples to reduce context pressure and improve tool use.
locator: Introduction; Tool Search Tool; Programmatic Tool Calling
notes: Anthropic Engineering article published 2025-11-24; internal performance figures are intentionally not generalized in this article.

claim: Anthropic recommends choosing tools deliberately, namespacing capabilities, returning meaningful and token-efficient context, and evaluating tool descriptions and behavior with agents.
MCP tools are discovered through tools/list and invoked through tools/call; the specification describes tools as model-controlled and recommends a human ability to deny invocations.
locator: User Interaction Model; Listing Tools; Calling Tools
notes: Protocol-level tool discovery and invocation do not themselves replace application authorization.

claim: OWASP recommends validating tool calls against user permissions, enforcing tool-specific parameter validation and least privilege, and treating retrieved/tool content as untrusted input.
locator: Agent-Specific Defenses; Least Privilege; Secure Implementation Pipeline
notes: Security guidance; defenses must be enforced at the execution boundary rather than by prompt wording alone.

claim: OpenAI recommends evaluating programmatic tool calling using task quality, evidence coverage, tokens, latency, cost, calls, retries, recovery and safety outcomes.
notes: Official platform guidance; article adapts these dimensions into a broader end-to-end tool-use checklist.

claim: OpenAI guardrail and human-review guidance distinguishes automatic validation from approval pauses before high-impact side effects.
locator: Choose the right control; human-in-the-loop approvals

claim: The interactive weather tool and Python executor use a fixed local fixture and an explicit allowlist; they are illustrative and do not access live weather or prove production authorization.
locator: Independent teaching example based on the documented tool-calling round trip
notes: Deterministic pedagogy; not a real API integration or benchmark.

claim: The success-probability decomposition is a conditional-probability chain-rule representation of tool selection, argument validity, execution and result integration.
locator: Independent pedagogical decomposition of the multi-step call flow
notes: No independence assumption is made; the terms are conditional probabilities.

claim: The sequential-versus-parallel latency equations are simplified explanatory models that omit queueing, orchestration, retries and service contention.
notes: Not a platform performance guarantee or measured benchmark.

claim: The five SVG figures are original diagrams illustrating the call loop, schema validation, parallel dependencies, tool ecosystem layers and security gates.
notes: Teaching diagrams, not reproduced figures from the cited papers or vendor documentation.
